title: 第18章 傻逼观众
content_zh:
谷川看马克沉默，掏出一叠美钞放进信封，然后走到马克身边，拽开他的口袋，就塞了进去。

    塞完之后，谷川就像是没事人一样，坐回原来的位置，继续谈版权的事情。

    “据我所知，《女巫布莱克》好像存在一些版权上的纠纷。”谷川说道。

    马克点了点头，毫不在意地说道：“不过是一些贪婪的演员，不知满足罢了。这只是小问题，影响不了什么。”

    “影响多大，可不是马克先生你说了算的。”

    “好吧。”马克说道：“这确实可能对以后造成影响，我给你减十万美元。”

    谷川再次起身。

    马克表情扭捏，口袋不自觉地就松了。

    等谷川再次落座，马克感觉沉甸甸的口袋，心中滋味难明。

    谷川又挑了好几个刺，马克一脸无奈地给谷川降价，看上去非常苦恼。

    一来二去，翻拍权已经降到十万美元以内了。

    “你知道的，我们很穷。”谷川说道。

    “好吧好吧，四万美元，真的不能再低了。”马克说道。

    “成交。”谷川点头。

    花四万美元买改编权，又给了马克三万美元。

    好多钱啊。

    小王给的钱根本不够用。

    ……

    2月2，《见鬼》正式上映。

    北航的郭威，一个人来到电影院，准备看看这个《见鬼》是怎么回事。

    他认为这是谣言，是一个炒作，但网上的傻伯夷太多了，他在论坛上和某人对喷了一百多楼，还准备线下约着碰一碰。

    郭威走进影院。

    如果这真的是诈骗，他就拿着钢管去和那个傻伯夷碰一碰，如果真的是纪录片，那只拿板砖就好了。

    ‘纪录片’缓缓放映。

    “艹！”

    郭威骂了一句。

    故事开头是一个深夜的乡村，沉重的铁门伴随着“吱呀”声缓缓推开，只有打火机微弱的火苗在颤抖，将周围扭曲的影子投射在斑驳的墙壁上。

    突然，黑暗中传来一声清晰的孩童笑声。

    镜头剧烈晃动了一下，火苗熄灭，画面瞬间陷入死寂。
content_en:
Seeing Mark's silence, Tanichuan took out a wad of U.S. dollars and put it in the envelope. Then he walked to Mark, opened his pocket, and stuffed it in.

    After finishing the stuffing, Tanichuan sat back to his original position as if nothing was wrong and continued to talk about copyright.

    "As far as I know, there seems to be some copyright disputes with "Witch Black"." Tanigawa said.

    Mark nodded and said nonchalantly: "They are just some greedy actors who are insatiable. This is just a small problem and will not affect anything."

    "Mr. Mark, it's not up to you to decide how big the impact will be."

    "Okay." Mark said, "This may indeed have an impact in the future. I'll give you a $100,000 discount."

    Tanichuan stood up again.

    Mark's expression was twisted, and his pockets became loose unconsciously.

    When Tanichuan sat down again, Mark felt his pockets were heavy, and his heart felt hard to understand.

    Tanichuan picked a few more thorns, and Mark reluctantly lowered the price for Tanichuan, looking very distressed.

    Over time, the remake rights have dropped to less than $100,000.

    "You know, we are poor," Tanigawa said.

    "Okay, okay, forty thousand dollars, it really can't go any lower," Mark said.

    "Deal." Tanichuan nodded.

    I spent $40,000 to buy the adaptation rights, and gave Mark another $30,000.

    That’s a lot of money.

    The money given by Xiao Wang was simply not enough.

    …

    On February 2, "Hell" was officially released.

    Guo Wei from Beihang University came to the cinema alone, ready to see what "Hell" was about.

    He thought it was a rumor and a hype, but there were too many idiots on the Internet. He argued with someone on the forum for more than a hundred floors, and was planning to meet offline.

    Guo Wei walked into the theater.

    If this was really a scam, he would have taken the steel pipe to touch that idiot Boyi. If it was really a documentary, he would have just taken the bricks.

    The ‘documentary’ plays slowly.

    "grass!"

    Guo Wei cursed.

    The story begins in a late-night countryside. The heavy iron door slowly opens with a "squeaking" sound. Only the weak flame of the lighter trembles, casting distorted shadows around it on the mottled walls.

    Suddenly, a clear child's laughter came from the darkness.

    The camera shook violently, the flames went out, and the scene fell into dead silence.
